subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: In a committee of 25 members, each member is proficient either in Mathematics or in Statistics or in both. If 19 of these are proficient in Mathematics, 16 in Statistics, find the probability that a person selected from the committee is proficient in both.

mark_split.label: Events and the counts; n(M ∪ S) = 25
n(M ∩ S) = n(M) + n(S) − n(M ∪ S)

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the probability that a member is proficient in both — what "either or both" tells you, the counting formula, and the answer.
insider_note: "Each member is proficient in either … or both" is the sentence that says the union is the whole committee, n(M ∪ St) = 25. Without reading it, the question cannot be started.

steps.label: Events and counts
steps.margin_note: First mark. Every member is in at least one group, so the union is all 25. Write the three counts.

lines.text: Every member is in M or St or both, so

recall.must_convey: That M and St are the two proficiency events, n(M) = 19, n(St) = 16, and because everyone is in at least one, n(M ∪ St) = 25.
accept: let M be maths and St be statistics, nineteen and sixteen, and since everyone is in at least one the union is twenty five
the union of the two groups is the whole committee of 25
n of M is 19, n of St is 16, n of union is 25
maths 19, statistics 16, andaru at least one lo unnaru kabatti union 25

steps.why: The counting version of the addition theorem needs n(M ∪ St); the phrase "either … or both" is what supplies it.
common_mistakes: Taking n(M ∪ St) = 19 + 16 = 35, which is more than the committee.

steps.label: Counting formula for the overlap
steps.margin_note: Second mark. n(M ∩ St) = n(M) + n(St) − n(M ∪ St) — the addition theorem in counts.

lines.text: n(M ∩ St) = n(M) + n(St) − n(M ∪ St)

recall.must_convey: That n(M ∩ St) = n(M) + n(St) − n(M ∪ St).
accept: the overlap count is n M plus n St minus n of the union
intersection equals sum of the two minus the union
use the addition formula on the counts
both count ante 19 plus 16 minus union

steps.why: Adding 19 and 16 counts the "both" members twice; subtracting the union, which counts them once, leaves exactly the overlap.
common_mistakes: Writing n(M ∩ St) = n(M ∪ St) − n(M) − n(St), the signs reversed.

steps.label: Compute and divide
steps.margin_note: Two marks. 19 + 16 − 25 = 10 members in both; probability = 10/25 = 2/5.

recall.must_convey: That n(M ∩ St) = 10 and the probability is 10/25 = 2/5.
accept: nineteen plus sixteen minus twenty five is ten, so ten by twenty five which is two fifths
ten members are in both, probability 2 by 5
the answer is two by five

steps.why: A probability is the favourable count over the total; the total here is the committee size.
